definition: Patient is aware of person (who they are), place (where they are), time (date/year), and event (why they are in the hospital).
nursingImplications: Baseline neuro assessment. Document A&Ox1–4. Sudden changes warrant provider notification and possible stroke workup.

term: Pupils Equal, Round, Reactive to Light
definition: Both pupils are the same size, circular, and constrict when light is shone.
nursingImplications: Abnormal pupils (unequal, non-reactive, blown) suggest increased intracranial pressure or CNS injury. Notify provider immediately.

definition: Neurological scale assessing eye opening (1–4), verbal response (1–5), and motor response (1–6). Max 15 = fully alert; below 8 indicates severe impairment.
nursingImplications: GCS ≤8 indicates intubation consideration. Serial GCS trending is more important than single value. Document each component.

definition: Patient is not to receive anything orally — no food, liquids, or oral medications (unless specified). Often ordered pre-operatively or when aspiration risk is present.
nursingImplications: Ensure IV access patent. Continue IV fluids as ordered. Hold oral meds unless cleared by provider. Provide oral care. Educate patient and family. Document last oral intake time.

definition: Diet consisting only of liquids you can see through at room temperature. Includes: water, clear broth, apple/white grape/cranberry juice, plain gelatin (Jell-O), popsicles, tea/coffee without cream, carbonated beverages.
nursingImplications: Does NOT include milk, orange juice, tomato juice, cream soups, or anything opaque. Monitor hydration. Often a step before advancing diet post-op.

definition: Diet low in sodium (<2g/day), saturated fats, trans fats, and cholesterol. Emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats.
nursingImplications: Educate patient on food label reading. Watch for hidden sodium. Common in CHF, HTN, CAD. Reinforce at every meal.

definition: Measures taken to prevent food/liquid from entering the airway. Includes proper positioning, appropriate food texture, HOB elevation, and swallowing evaluation.
nursingImplications: HOB at 30–90° during and 30–60 min after meals. Refer to speech therapy for dysphagia eval. Document consistency: thin liquid, nectar-thick, honey-thick, pureed. Keep suction at bedside.

definition: The top number of a blood pressure reading representing the pressure when the heart contracts and pumps blood.
nursingImplications: Normal adult SBP: 90–120 mmHg. Hold most antihypertensives if SBP <90. Notify provider of SBP <90 or >180 in most circumstances.

definition: Peripheral pulse oximetry reading representing the percentage of hemoglobin saturated with oxygen.
nursingImplications: Goal usually ≥92–95% for most patients, 88–92% for COPD patients (hypoxic drive). Verify with ABG if SpO2 unreliable. Assess nail polish, perfusion, probe placement.

definition: Blood test measuring how long it takes for blood to clot via the intrinsic pathway. Used to monitor heparin infusions.
nursingImplications: Therapeutic range for heparin: typically 60–100 seconds (per facility protocol). Obtain 6h after initiating heparin, 6h after every rate change, then q6h when stable. Critical value >120s → hold heparin, notify provider.

definition: Immune-mediated reaction to heparin causing platelet activation and paradoxical thrombosis despite low platelet counts. Life-threatening.
nursingImplications: Monitor platelet count on heparin. 4T score assessment. If suspected: stop all heparin (including flushes), notify provider STAT, switch to alternative anticoagulant (argatroban, fondaparinux). Never restart heparin.

definition: Standardized measure of the extrinsic clotting pathway. Used to monitor warfarin therapy.
nursingImplications: Therapeutic INR for most indications: 2.0–3.0 (mechanical valves: 2.5–3.5). INR >4: hold warfarin, notify provider. Assess for bleeding. Vitamin K available for reversal.

definition: Hormone released by ventricles in response to stretching from volume overload. Elevated in heart failure.
nursingImplications: BNP >100 pg/mL suggests HF. Trending values more meaningful than single result. Used alongside clinical assessment (JVD, edema, crackles, dyspnea). Guides diuresis.

definition: Byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, elevated when tissues are not receiving adequate oxygen (tissue hypoperfusion, sepsis).
nursingImplications: Normal <2 mmol/L. Lactate ≥2 = elevated; ≥4 = severe sepsis. Repeat q2–4h until trending down. Drives fluid resuscitation and antibiotic urgency per sepsis protocol.

definition: Waste product filtered by the kidneys. Elevated creatinine indicates reduced kidney filtration (AKI or CKD).
nursingImplications: Trend creatinine. Hold nephrotoxic meds (NSAIDs, metformin, contrast-related meds) if rising. Strict I&Os. Assess urine output (goal ≥0.5 mL/kg/hr). Notify provider if acute rise.

definition: Closed-suction drain placed surgically to remove fluid (blood, serum, lymphatic fluid) from a wound or body cavity. Uses a compressible bulb to create negative pressure.
nursingImplications: Strip tubing to maintain patency. Empty and re-compress bulb when half full. Document output amount, color, consistency q shift. Notify provider if output suddenly increases (>100 mL/hr) or has frank blood.

definition: Advanced wound care system using sub-atmospheric pressure (vacuum) applied via foam/gauze interface and sealed dressing to promote wound healing, reduce edema, and remove exudate.
nursingImplications: Check seal integrity q2h — listen/feel for air leak. Common settings: -75 to -125 mmHg continuous or intermittent. Record canister output. Change dressing per order (typically q48–72h). Assess surrounding skin. Alarm troubleshooting: check tubing, dressing edges, canister level.

definition: Concentrated red blood cells separated from plasma. Used to increase oxygen-carrying capacity in anemia or hemorrhage.
nursingImplications: Two-nurse verification. Type & screen / crossmatch required. Infuse over 2–4h per unit (max 4h). VS baseline, 15 min, 30 min, q1h, and post-infusion. First 15 min: stay with patient. Stop transfusion immediately if reaction suspected. Transfusion reactions: fever, chills, rash, hypotension, flank pain, dyspnea.

definition: Plasma containing all clotting factors. Used to reverse coagulopathy, warfarin overdose, or prior to invasive procedures in coagulopathic patients.
nursingImplications: Two-nurse verify. ABO compatible (does not require crossmatch). Infuse promptly after thawing (within 24h if stored at 1–6°C). Monitor for volume overload (TACO) and TRALI. VS monitoring same as PRBCs.

definition: Blood components essential for clot formation. Transfused when platelet count is critically low (<10,000) or patient is bleeding with low counts (<50,000 for procedures).
nursingImplications: Infuse rapidly (over 15–30 min). ABO compatible preferred. Two-nurse verify. Monitor post-transfusion platelet count (expect ~10,000 increase per unit). Watch for febrile non-hemolytic reactions (most common transfusion reaction with platelets).

definition: Blood product derived from FFP containing concentrated fibrinogen, Factor VIII, Factor XIII, vWF, and fibronectin. Used for fibrinogen replacement in DIC, massive hemorrhage.
nursingImplications: Infuse within 4h of thaw. Small volume but given rapidly. Monitor fibrinogen levels. Two-nurse verify. ABO compatibility not required.

definition: Distension of the jugular veins visible at >45° head-of-bed elevation, indicating elevated right heart pressures or volume overload.
nursingImplications: Measure at 45° HOB. JVD >3–4 cm above sternal angle is significant. Associated with CHF, cardiac tamponade, tension pneumothorax, SVC syndrome. Document and report.

definition: Edema that retains an indentation (pit) when pressed. Graded 1+ (2mm) to 4+ (>8mm). Indicates excess interstitial fluid.
nursingImplications: Document grade, location (bilateral LE, sacral, periorbital). Monitor daily weights. Strict I&Os. Diuretics usually ordered. Elevate affected extremities. Assess skin integrity.

definition: Non-invasive measurement of oxygen saturation via pulse oximetry sensor.
nursingImplications: Verify accuracy: nail polish, poor perfusion, motion, hypothermia reduce accuracy. Correlate with clinical picture. If suspicious, confirm with ABG. Titrate supplemental O2 to goal.

definition: Irregular, often rapid heart rhythm caused by chaotic electrical activity in the atria. Absent P waves and irregularly irregular rhythm on ECG.
nursingImplications: Rate control goal typically <110 bpm (or <80 if symptomatic). Rhythm control per order. Assess for hemodynamic instability. Anticoagulation for stroke prevention. Monitor for new onset — may need urgent rate control.

definition: Life-threatening complication of diabetes marked by hyperglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and ketonemia due to profound insulin deficiency.
nursingImplications: Fluid resuscitation (NS or LR). Insulin drip per protocol. Monitor glucose q1h. Potassium replacement critical (check K+ before starting insulin). Watch for cerebral edema, hypoglycemia. Identify precipitating cause.

definition: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by dysregulated host response to infection. SIRS + suspected infection + organ dysfunction (SOFA ≥2).
nursingImplications: 1-hour bundle: blood cultures x2, lactate, broad-spectrum antibiotics, 30 mL/kg IV fluid for hypotension. Reassess fluid responsiveness. Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP <65. Strict I&Os, hourly urine output.

definition: Clinical syndrome in which the heart cannot pump sufficient blood to meet the body's demands, leading to fluid congestion in lungs, extremities, or both.
nursingImplications: Daily weights (same time, same scale, same clothing). Strict I&Os. Sodium restriction. Diuretics, ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers per order. Monitor BNP, renal function. O2 supplementation. HOB elevation for dyspnea. Educate on fluid/sodium restriction.

definition: Sudden decrease in kidney function over hours to days. Classified as pre-renal (decreased perfusion), intrinsic (kidney damage), or post-renal (obstruction).
nursingImplications: Strict I&Os, hourly urine output (goal ≥0.5 mL/kg/hr). Trending creatinine, BUN. Avoid nephrotoxins. Hold metformin, NSAIDs, contrast agents. Medication dose adjustments needed. Dialysis may be required.

definition: Blockage of a pulmonary artery by a blood clot, fat, or air, impairing gas exchange. Most often from DVT.
nursingImplications: Sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia, decreased SpO2. Supplemental O2. Anticoagulation per order (heparin, LMWH, or direct oral anticoagulants). Massive PE may require thrombolytics. Monitor for bleeding.

definition: Blood clot (thrombus) in a deep vein, most commonly in the leg. Risk factors: immobility, surgery, malignancy, hypercoagulability.
nursingImplications: Unilateral leg swelling, warmth, erythema, calf pain (Homan's sign unreliable). Anticoagulation per order. SCDs/TED hose for prophylaxis. Early ambulation. Monitor for PE conversion.

definition: Sudden neurological deficit caused by ischemic infarct (87%) or hemorrhagic event in the brain.
nursingImplications: FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call. Activate stroke alert per protocol. NIH Stroke Scale. CT head immediately. tPA eligibility window 3–4.5h from symptom onset for ischemic stroke (no hemorrhage confirmed). Strict BP management.

definition: Closed-suction wound drain using a flat, disc-shaped reservoir that creates negative pressure. Used post-operatively to remove fluid from surgical sites.
nursingImplications: Empty when reservoir is half full. Compress flat to re-establish suction. Secure tubing to avoid tension. Document output color and amount. Notify provider of output >100mL/hr or sudden increase.

definition: Hollow plastic tube inserted into the pleural space to drain air (pneumothorax), blood (hemothorax), or fluid (pleural effusion).
nursingImplications: Water-seal chamber must remain below patient. Tidal fluctuation in water-seal (tidaling) indicates patent tube. Continuous bubbling in water-seal = air leak. Mark drainage q shift. Keep system upright. Two clamps at bedside. Notify provider for sudden cessation of drainage, tension pneumothorax signs, or >200 mL/hr output.

definition: Dangerous increase in pressure within a closed muscle compartment, compromising blood flow. Surgical emergency.
nursingImplications: 6 P's: Pain (disproportionate, especially with passive stretch), Pressure (tenseness), Pallor, Paresthesia, Paralysis, Pulselessness (late sign). NOTIFY PROVIDER IMMEDIATELY. Never elevate limb above heart level. Emergency fasciotomy required. Document neuro checks q1–2h for cast patients.

definition: Assessment of circulation, sensation, and movement distal to a cast, splint, or injury. Critical for detecting compartment syndrome.
nursingImplications: Assess q1–2h for acute casts. Compare bilateral. 5 P's minimum: Pain, Pulse, Paresthesia, Paralysis, Pallor (+ capillary refill). Document and immediately report any changes from baseline.

definition: Breathing device used post-operatively to encourage deep breaths and prevent atelectasis.
nursingImplications: Goal: 10 breaths/hr while awake. Hold inspiratory volume 3–5 seconds. Sit upright. Splint incision with pillow. Document highest volume achieved. Encourage coughing after deep breaths.

definition: Pneumatic compression sleeves placed on calves that cyclically inflate to prevent DVT via mechanical compression and fibrinolytic stimulation.
nursingImplications: Remove for ambulation, assessment, skin care. Ensure proper fit and placement. Check skin under device q8h. Contraindicated in DVT, peripheral arterial disease, leg fractures/wounds.

definition: Major intracellular cation critical for cardiac and neuromuscular function. Normal serum level: 3.5–5.0 mEq/L.
nursingImplications: Hypokalemia (<3.5): muscle weakness, cramps, cardiac arrhythmias. Hyperkalemia (>5.0): peaked T waves, cardiac arrest. Replace per order (oral preferred if tolerating; IV must be diluted and infused slowly — never IV push). Monitor EKG.

definition: Major extracellular cation regulating fluid balance, nerve/muscle function. Normal: 135–145 mEq/L.
nursingImplications: Hyponatremia: confusion, seizures (if severe, <120). Correct slowly (≤10 mEq/24h) to prevent osmotic demyelination syndrome. Hypernatremia: thirst, lethargy, seizures. Free water replacement. Monitor neuro status.

definition: Position of the patient's head end of the bed, expressed in degrees.
nursingImplications: HOB ≥30° for ventilated patients (VAP bundle), aspiration precautions, post-feeding, and GERD. HOB flat for spinal precautions, hypotension. Document position for relevant orders.

definition: Medication or intervention ordered to be given when needed based on patient assessment, not on a fixed schedule.
nursingImplications: Assess patient need before administration. Document indication, time given, patient response. For pain: reassess 30–60 min after oral, 15–30 min after IV/IM administration.

definition: Documentation of all fluid taken in (oral, IV, tube feeds) and all fluid output (urine, drains, emesis, stool) over a period, typically 8 or 12 hours.
nursingImplications: Accurate I&Os are critical for volume assessment in CHF, AKI, sepsis, post-op. Goal urine output ≥0.5 mL/kg/hr. Report urine output <30 mL/hr for two consecutive hours.

definition: Continuous cardiac monitoring via electrode leads transmitting rhythm data to a central station.
nursingImplications: Assess rhythm q4–8h. Document any changes. Verify leads attached and signal clear. Identify: rate, rhythm, P waves, PR interval, QRS, QT interval. Report new arrhythmias per protocol.

definition: Discontinuous, adventitious lung sounds heard on auscultation, caused by fluid in alveoli or opening of collapsed airways.
nursingImplications: Fine crackles: early CHF, pulmonary fibrosis. Coarse crackles: pneumonia, pulmonary edema. Document location. Position HOB up. Notify provider if new or worsening with dyspnea.

definition: High-pitched whistling sound on expiration (occasionally inspiration) caused by narrowed airways.
nursingImplications: Asthma, COPD exacerbation, anaphylaxis, foreign body. Administer bronchodilators per order. Assess respiratory status, SpO2. Notify provider if new or severe. Keep epinephrine available if anaphylaxis suspected.

definition: Head, Eyes, Ears, Nose, Throat assessment.
nursingImplications: Standard assessment abbreviation. Document findings per system. Relevant for stroke (eye deviation, facial droop), ENT infections, head injuries.

definition: Sounds heard on abdominal auscultation created by peristalsis. Described as present, absent, hypoactive, or hyperactive.
nursingImplications: Auscultate all 4 quadrants before palpation. Absent BS for >5 min in all quadrants = absent (ileus concern). Hyperactive: diarrhea, early obstruction. Absent: ileus, peritonitis. Document and report significant changes.

definition: Nitrogen-containing waste product from protein metabolism, cleared by the kidneys. Normal: 7–20 mg/dL.
nursingImplications: Elevated in AKI, CKD, dehydration, GI bleeding, high protein intake. BUN:Cr ratio >20:1 suggests pre-renal cause. Trend alongside creatinine.

definition: Blood test identifying patient's ABO blood type, Rh factor, and screening for irregular antibodies. Required before blood product administration.
nursingImplications: Usually required before surgery or anticipated transfusion. Different from crossmatch (T&S alone does not release blood). Two-person verification of patient ID at time of draw critical to prevent hemolytic transfusion reaction.

definition: Blood typing plus compatibility testing of donor blood against recipient's blood. Specific units held for patient use.
nursingImplications: Required for scheduled blood transfusions. Units held for 72h (varies by facility). Two-person ID verification mandatory at bedside before initiating transfusion.

definition: Continuous infusion of sterile irrigant (usually normal saline) through a three-way Foley catheter to prevent clot formation in the bladder post-urologic surgery.
nursingImplications: Monitor output color (should lighten over time). Decrease rate if brightening; increase if darkening or clots present. Report: frank red blood, inability to drain, blocked catheter despite flushing, patient discomfort or spasm.

definition: Flexible tube inserted through the nose into the stomach. Used for decompression (suctioning stomach contents) or enteral feeding.
nursingImplications: Verify placement before any use: pH <5 preferred, bedside X-ray gold standard. Mark tube at nostril. Irrigate per order. If suction: document output color and amount. Assess nares and mucosa q shift. HOB 30–45° for feeds.

definition: Communication framework: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation. Standard tool for structured patient handoff and provider communication.
nursingImplications: Use for all provider calls, handoffs, and transfers. Clear, concise, complete. State recommendation specifically. Document that provider was notified and any orders received.

definition: Patient weight measured each morning under standardized conditions (same scale, same time, same clothing).
nursingImplications: Critical in CHF, renal failure, liver disease. 1 kg ≈ 1 liter of fluid. Report weight gain >2 lbs (0.9 kg) in 24h or >5 lbs in 1 week to provider. Document consistently.

definition: Specimen drawn from peripheral vein (not IV line) and sent to lab to identify microorganisms in the bloodstream (bacteremia/septicemia).
nursingImplications: Draw 2 sets from 2 different sites BEFORE antibiotics. Use sterile technique. Timing: within 1 hour of identifying sepsis criteria. Document time drawn and antibiotic start time. Incubation takes 48–72h.

definition: Percentage of blood volume composed of red blood cells. Normal: Male 41–53%, Female 36–46%.
nursingImplications: Low Hct indicates anemia, blood loss. Monitor alongside Hgb. Transfusion threshold typically Hgb <7–8 g/dL (or higher with symptoms/cardiac history). Trending more important than single value.

definition: Oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. Normal: Male 13.5–17.5 g/dL, Female 12.0–15.5 g/dL.
nursingImplications: Monitor for symptomatic anemia (fatigue, dyspnea, tachycardia). Transfusion usually considered Hgb <7 g/dL in stable patients, <8 in cardiac patients. Check pre- and post-transfusion (expect ~1 g/dL rise per unit PRBCs).

definition: Total count of white blood cells (immune cells) in the blood. Normal: 4,500–11,000 cells/μL.
nursingImplications: Elevated WBC (leukocytosis): infection, inflammation, leukemia. Decreased WBC (leukopenia): immunosuppression risk. Monitor neutrophil count (ANC) in immunocompromised patients. Trending with temperature and clinical picture guides sepsis management.

definition: Cardiac-specific protein released when myocardial cells are damaged. Elevated in myocardial infarction, myocarditis, PE, and other conditions causing cardiac stress.
nursingImplications: Serial troponins q3–6h x2–3 per protocol for ACS workup. Rising or falling pattern with clinical context is diagnostic. Notify provider of positive or rising troponin. Keep patient on continuous monitoring. Pain management.
